slowest_experiments.label: Exp 53: Runtime constraint instrumentation
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Early-milestone infrastructure experiment with no prior tooling; required building the constraint instrumentation framework from scratch. This same experiment appeared as the top outlier in the 2026.04.18 retro — root cause was never addressed because the fix (milestone cold-start scaffolding template) was recommended but not implemented before this milestone began.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 219: Live GSM8K semantic benchmark on Qwen3.5-0.8B and Gemma
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Sequential model loading — Qwen then Gemma loaded into a single GPU one at a time. DualGPURunner was not wired until Exp 258 (near milestone end), so this experiment ran with only one GPU active. No inference batching; each of the 200 GSM8K cases was a single forward pass.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 184: 3B model verification — does verify-repair help large models
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: 3B-parameter model requires significantly more VRAM and per-call inference time than the 0.8B baseline. The verify-repair loop multiplied forward passes (baseline → verify → repair → re-verify) on a single GPU with no batching. Second GPU was idle throughout.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 221: Live prompt-side constraint benchmark on typed IR tasks
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Typed IR generation pipeline ran sequentially across prompt variants; constraint evaluation was single-threaded with no batching. Candidate for DualGPUBenchmarkHarness parallelization now that Exp 258 harness is available.

slowest_experiments.label: Exp 155: Retrain JEPA violation predictor v2 with multi-domain data
slowest_experiments.likely_cause: Multi-domain retraining required full dataset reload and feature extraction for each domain in sequence on CPU only (JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu). No GPU training pipeline was invoked. Correct for reproducibility, but the corpus was large enough that batched CPU parallelism (e.g., multiprocessing across domains) would have helped.

bottlenecks_identified: CARRY-OVER: Prior retro recommendations went unimplemented. All 5 of the slowest experiments in this milestone were identical to those flagged in the 2026.04.18 retro. Retro action items were written as suggestions rather than tracked tickets — zero were resolved before this milestone started.

DualGPURunner wired too late: Exp 258 (dual-GPU harness) and Exp 260 (GPU-accelerated benchmark) were experiments 258 and 260 of 280. Only the final 0.7% of experiments benefited from dual-GPU parallelization. The remaining 99.3% ran on a single GPU or CPU with the second RTX 3090 idle.

Sequential model loading persists for all pre-258 experiments: both RTX 3090s never ran simultaneously for any experiment before Exp 258. At 14 min/experiment average, ~251 experiments × ~40% involving two models = roughly 100 GPU-hours of second-GPU idle time.

CUDA ORT kernel-launch overhead discovered late (Exp 257-259): GPU is 5.49× slower than CPU ORT for the 9→1 linear gate at batch_size=1. This finding should have been discovered in a micro-benchmark at milestone start rather than consuming Exp 257-259 near the end.

Inference batching still absent: Exp 260 showed ~33s/case for verify_repair on GPU — still one case per forward pass. Batch inference at batch_size=8–16 would reduce this to ~4–6s/case for the same GPU.

Doc provenance drift triggered repeated full 2500-test suite runs: the changelog shows at least 6 separate doc-sync passes (provenance inventory reconciliation, milestone count, test_docs fixes) each triggering the full test suite. Estimated 6 × 90s = 9 minutes of avoidable test overhead, plus multiple conductor turns consumed.

Zombie/residual VRAM allocations not cleaned up: both GPUs show 2MB allocated at 0% utilization at milestone end — same pattern as 2026.04.18 (4–5MB residual). The gpu_monitor --kill-zombies teardown hook was recommended in the prior retro but not added to the conductor teardown sequence.

Pre-flight test suite run for non-code changes: several changelog entries show the full 2500-test suite run after documentation-only or results-only changes (README, docs/index.html, ops/status.md). A doc-only classifier would have run 5 tests instead of 2500.

Checkpoint granularity coarse on long experiments: Exp 260 shows per-model/per-mode cell checkpointing (6 Qwen GSM8K cells) but not per-question. A single failure mid-run requires replaying the whole cell rather than resuming at the last question.

gpu_monitor.py was not running continuously during the milestone: peak GPU utilization is unknown. The 2026.04.18 retro flagged this; it was not addressed. Without continuous logging, bottleneck analysis is inference-only.
improvements_suggested: Convert retro action items to tracked tasks: create a story in epics/stories/ for each retro action item before the next milestone begins. Recommendations that are not committed to tracked tickets will not be acted on — this milestone is proof.

Wire DualGPURunner at experiment 1, not experiment 258: add DualGPUBenchmarkHarness as the default scheduler for any experiment that references more than one model. Estimated throughput gain: 1.7–2.0x for paired-model benchmarks (40% of experiments).

Add per-question checkpointing to all live inference loops: checkpoint every 10 questions within a cell, not just at cell boundaries. Cuts worst-case restart cost for Exp 219-class experiments from 117 min to ~12 min.

Add a doc-only test classifier to the conductor: if `git diff --name-only HEAD` touches only README.md, docs/, ops/, results/*.json, _bmad/traceability.md — run only tests/python/test_docs.py (5 tests, ~1s) instead of the full 2500-test suite. This alone would have saved ~6 conductor turns this milestone.

Add a provenance auto-sync pre-commit hook: script that counts results/experiment_*_results.json files and writes the count into README.md and docs/index.html before every commit, so the provenance inventory never drifts.

Add gpu_monitor.py to conductor teardown sequence: call python scripts/gpu_monitor.py --kill-zombies --dry-run after each experiment; on zombie detection, kill and log before starting the next experiment. Also add --loop --interval 60 as a background process at conductor start for continuous utilization logging.

Determine GPU batch threshold at milestone start: run the CUDA ORT micro-benchmark (now available as Exp 259) on day 1 of each milestone to confirm whether GPU or CPU is faster for the current gate size. Exp 257-259 would have been one early experiment rather than three near-end ones.

Add batched inference harness for all live benchmark loops: replace the per-case forward-pass loop with a batched call (batch_size=8 via CARNOT_DUAL_GPU_BATCH_SIZE). Exp 260 at ~33s/case → ~4–6s/case projected. Applies to GSM8K, HumanEval, and constraint_ir harnesses.

Add a milestone cold-start scaffolding template: a ready-to-go experiment script skeleton with DualGPUBenchmarkHarness, checkpoint helpers, and artifact schema so Exp 1 of the next milestone reuses infrastructure rather than rebuilding it (targets the 418-minute Exp-53 outlier pattern).

Add a parallelism planner to the conductor: group experiments with no data dependencies and dispatch them concurrently on separate GPUs or CPU cores. Even a simple dependency-graph pass would allow 2–3 independent experiments to run simultaneously.
Run gpu_monitor.py in continuous --loop --interval 60 mode from conductor start: write timestamped JSON logs to results/gpu_utilization_YYYYMMDD.jsonl so peak utilization is known, not estimated.

time_savings_breakdown.note: Estimates assume 280 experiments of similar composition. DualGPU gain applies to ~40% of experiments running paired models. Batching gain applies to ~60% with live inference. Checkpoint granularity saves restart cost on long experiments (~5% of experiment count, ~15% of wall time). Savings are multiplicative in practice — these are additive lower bounds.

delta_vs_prior_milestone.key_new_finding: CUDA ORT is 5.49× SLOWER than CPU ORT for a 9→1 gate at batch_size=1 (Exp 259). GPU advantage only appears at batch_size ≥ 32. This inverts the assumed GPU-always-faster default and means the correct strategy is: CPU ORT gate + GPU LLM inference + batched queries.

Marginally improved vs 2026.04.18 (4–5MB residual) but still not zero. No continuous utilization log was collected, so peak GPU use during the milestone is unknown.
